item.description: One midnight in 2007, a Chinese factory foreman woke 8,000 workers in their dormitories. item.title: How will China’s ties with Myanmar change with the ICJ’s genocide ruling?
item.description: An international court ruling of genocide against Myanmar might complicate Beijing’s diplomatic engagement with Naypyidaw and cast a shadow over Belt and Road Initiative infrastructure projects in the country, observers warn. The landmark decision by the UN’s highest judicial body covers Myanmar’s 2017 military campaign against the majority-Muslim Rohingya minority in Rakhine state that killed at least 10,000 people and forced hundreds of thousands more to flee. item.title: Chinese state media hits out at ‘deflation trap’ warnings, defends economic performance
item.description: Communist Party mouthpiece People’s Daily has pushed back against Western descriptions of China’s economy, including claims of a “deflation trap” and “China Shock 2.0”, accusing critics of seeking to undermine confidence in the country and justify trade restrictions. The remarks came as some economists forecast that China’s full-year growth would register near the lower end of Beijing’s official 4.5 to 5 per cent target range this year. item.title: As brain-computer interface boom enters next phase, China pushes to shape global standards
item.description: China will set up a new standard-setting task force for brain-computer interface (BCI) technologies, while a state-backed think tank has urged investors to remain patient as the nascent but increasingly crowded sector develops.
